name: Israel's Disc Source of the Kerr Metric
description: Kerr's spacetime cut at the disc spanning its ring singularity, the sheet of negative $r$ thrown away and the two faces of the disc glued together, as Werner Israel did in 1970. The seam carries a layer of negative mass turning faster than light, and the spacetime keeps only the causal part of Kerr's extension.
convention: We keep factors of $c$ explicit; the mass enters as the length $m = GM/c^2$ and the spin per unit mass $a$ is a length. The Ricci tensor is the standard contraction, $R_{\mu\nu} = R^\alpha{}_{\mu\alpha\nu}$.
history: In the coordinates of Robert Boyer and Richard Lindquist, the ring singularity of Kerr's spacetime bounds a flat disc of radius $a$ where $r = 0$ [kerr1963, boyer1967]. A path through the disc carries on to negative $r$, a second sheet of the spacetime joined to the first along that disc [boyer1967]. Brandon Carter followed the extension through and found closed timelike lines near the ring in every case but the spherical one [carter1968].¶Werner Israel, in the Mathematics Department of the University of Alberta in Edmonton, cut the spacetime at the disc in 1970 [israel1970]. He kept the sheet of positive $r$ alone and glued the upper face of the disc to the lower, so that a path through the disc comes out on the far side of the same sheet. The field is continuous across the seam and its normal derivatives jump, and Israel took the jump to be the field of a layer of mass and charge spread over the disc, which he computed for the charged Kerr-Newman metric and for Kerr's [israel1970]. For the uncharged metric the cut removes the noncausal parts of the manifold, and the layer is "the unique source of the causally maximal extension of the vacuum metric" [israel1970]. He set beside it a Newtonian field with the same source on the same disc [israel1970]. Its particle orbits avoid the ring as Kerr's geodesics do, and in the charged case the gyromagnetic ratio of the field, the Dirac electron's, shows in the character of the layer [israel1970].¶Nothing ordinary behaves like this layer. At a distance $\rho$ from the centre of the disc it carries a surface mass density $-\frac{ma}{2\pi(a^2-\rho^2)^{3/2}}$, negative everywhere and growing without bound at the rim, so the ring itself has to hold an infinite positive mass for the whole to weigh $m$ [bianchi2025]. The matter streams round at $a/\rho$ times the speed of light: at light speed on the rim, faster than light everywhere inside it, and faster without bound toward the centre. An observer carried round rigidly at angular velocity $c/a$ measures zero energy density anywhere on the disc. With $m = 0$ the layer vanishes and the cut spacetime is flat, while the whole of Kerr's spacetime at $m = 0$ is a wormhole held open by a ring of negative tension, as Gary Gibbons and Mikhail Volkov showed in 2017 [gibbons2017].¶Jiří Bičák and Tomáš Ledvinka found discs of plausible matter for Kerr's metric in 1993 [bicak1993kerr]. They cut the spacetime on two planes, one above the ring and one below, and glued the planes together, leaving out the slab between them and the ring inside it [bicak2000]. The seam carries two streams of particles circling in opposite senses at different speeds, a disc reaching to infinity with a finite mass, and for every type of Kerr metric it can hold ergoregions, flows close to light speed and redshifts as large as one likes [bicak1993kerr, bicak2000].¶Herbert Balasin and Herbert Nachbagauer wrote down the energy momentum tensor of Kerr and Newman's metrics in 1994 as a distribution over the whole of space, and found it lives on the disc of radius $a$ [balasin1994]. For every test function that vanishes on the ring it agrees with Israel's layer [balasin1994]. Massimo Bianchi, Claudio Gambino, Paolo Pani and Fabio Riccioni reached the same disc in 2025 from a mass, an angular momentum and the tower of Kerr's multipole moments, at linear order in the gravitational coupling, and found Israel's surface density in perfect agreement [bianchi2025].

related.text: Kerr's spacetime is what the disc source is cut from. Keep its sheet of positive $r$, glue the upper face of the disc in its ring to the lower, and the seam carries Israel's layer [israel1970].
With $m = 0$ the layer on the disc vanishes and the cut spacetime is flat, written in oblate spheroidal coordinates [gibbons2017].
With $a = 0$ the disc shrinks to the point $r = 0$ and the spacetime is Schwarzschild's.
Israel cut the charged Kerr-Newman metric at its disc in the same way, and found a layer of mass and charge that carries the Dirac electron's gyromagnetic ratio [israel1970].
Thin discs as the sources of vacuum fields. Jiří Bičák and Tomáš Ledvinka built discs of two counterrotating streams for Kerr's metric by the same cut and glue [bicak1993kerr, bicak2000].
Werner Israel's surface layers again: a field that is continuous across a surface while its normal derivatives jump, and a sheet of matter on the surface to carry the jump.
Spacetimes cut and glued, with all their matter on the seam. The seam's matter is exotic in both, negative mass on the disc and negative energy density on the throat.

coordinates.name: Boyer-Lindquist
domains: (r, \theta) = (0, \theta) \sim (0, \pi - \theta) \;\text{(the two faces of the disc, one surface)}
\Delta = 0 \;\text{(the horizons } r_\pm = m \pm \sqrt{m^2 - a^2}\text{, for } a \le m\text{)}
\Sigma = 0 \;\text{(the ring singularity, the rim of the disc)}

parameters.description: Spin per unit mass, $a = J/(Mc)$, a length and the radius of the disc; horizons exist for $a \le m$
Vanishes only on the ring $r = 0$, $\theta = \pi/2$, the rim of the disc
Its roots are the horizons $r_\pm = m \pm \sqrt{m^2 - a^2}$, which exist for $a \le m$

coordinates.convention: We use the coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \phi)$ of Boyer and Lindquist, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time, and keep only $r \ge 0$. The disc $r = 0$ is the flat disc of radius $a$ spanning the ring, and its upper face $\theta < \pi/2$ is the same surface as its lower face, the point at $\theta$ joined to the point at $\pi - \theta$. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/d\lambda$.

coordinates.name: Kerr-Schild
domains: (r, \theta) = (0, \theta) \sim (0, \pi - \theta) \;\text{(the two faces of the disc, one surface)}
\Sigma = 0 \;\text{(the ring singularity, the rim of the disc)}

parameters.description: Spin per unit mass, $a = J/(Mc)$, a length and the radius of the disc; horizons exist for $a \le m$
Vanishes only on the ring $r = 0$, $\theta = \pi/2$, the rim of the disc
Its roots are the horizons $r_\pm = m \pm \sqrt{m^2 - a^2}$, which exist for $a \le m$

coordinates.convention: We use Kerr and Schild's form in spheroidal coordinates $(\tau, r, \theta, \psi)$, flat space in oblate spheroidal coordinates plus $2mr/\Sigma$ times the square of a null one form, with $\tau$ carrying dimensions of time and $c\,d\tau = c\,dt + 2mr\,dr/\Delta$, $d\psi = d\phi + 2mar\,dr/\left(\left(r^2 + a^2\right)\Delta\right)$. The chart runs through both horizons to the disc $r = 0$, whose two faces are joined as in Boyer and Lindquist's chart. We take components in the chart $x^0 = c\tau$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter.

nonzero.value: \dfrac{r\,\Sigma^2\left(r^2 + a^2\right) - m\,a^2\left(3r^4 + a^2\,r^2\cos^2\theta + a^2\,r^2 - a^4\cos^2\theta\right)\sin^2\theta - 2m^2\,a^2\,r\left(r^2 - a^2\cos^2\theta\right)\sin^2\theta}{\Sigma^2\left(r^2 + a^2\right)^2}

\dfrac{r\,\Sigma^2\left(r^2 + a^2\right) - m\,a^2\left(3r^4 + a^2\,r^2\cos^2\theta + a^2\,r^2 - a^4\cos^2\theta\right)\sin^2\theta - 2m^2\,a^2\,r\left(r^2 - a^2\cos^2\theta\right)\sin^2\theta}{\Sigma^2\left(r^2 + a^2\right)^2}

geodesics: \ddot{\tau} + \dfrac{2m^2\,r\left(r^2 - a^2\cos^2\theta\right)}{\Sigma^3}\dot{\tau}^2 + \dfrac{2m\left(r^2 - a^2\cos^2\theta\right)\left(r^2 + a^2 + 2m\,r\right)}{\Sigma^2\left(r^2 + a^2\right)}\dot{\tau}\dot{r} - \dfrac{4m\,a^2\,r\sin\theta\cos\theta}{\Sigma^2}\dot{\tau}\dot{\theta} - \dfrac{4m^2\,a\,r\left(r^2 - a^2\cos^2\theta\right)\sin^2\theta}{\Sigma^3}\dot{\tau}\dot{\psi} + \dfrac{2m\left(r^4 - a^4\cos^2\theta + m\,r^3 - m\,a^2\,r\cos^2\theta\right)}{\Sigma\left(r^2 + a^2\right)^2}\dot{r}^2 - \dfrac{4m\,a^2\,r\sin\theta\cos\theta}{\Sigma\left(r^2 + a^2\right)}\dot{r}\dot{\theta} - \dfrac{2m\,a\left(4r^4 + 2a^2\,r^2 - 2a^4\cos^2\theta - \Delta\left(r^2 - a^2\cos^2\theta\right)\right)\sin^2\theta}{\Sigma^2\left(r^2 + a^2\right)}\dot{r}\dot{\psi} - \dfrac{2m\,r^2}{\Sigma}\dot{\theta}^2 + \dfrac{4m\,a^3\,r\sin^3\theta\cos\theta}{\Sigma^2}\dot{\theta}\dot{\psi} - \dfrac{2m\,r\left(r\,\Sigma^2 - m\,a^2\left(r^2 - a^2\cos^2\theta\right)\sin^2\theta\right)\sin^2\theta}{\Sigma^3}\dot{\psi}^2 = 0

\ddot{r} + \dfrac{m\,\Delta\left(r^2 - a^2\cos^2\theta\right)}{\Sigma^3}\dot{\tau}^2 - \dfrac{4m^2\,r\left(r^2 - a^2\cos^2\theta\right)}{\Sigma^2\left(r^2 + a^2\right)}\dot{\tau}\dot{r} - \dfrac{2m\,a\,\Delta\left(r^2 - a^2\cos^2\theta\right)\sin^2\theta}{\Sigma^3}\dot{\tau}\dot{\psi} + \dfrac{\left(a^2\,r\sin^2\theta - m\left(r^2 - a^2\cos^2\theta\right)\right)\left(r^2 + a^2 + 2m\,r\right)}{\Sigma\left(r^2 + a^2\right)^2}\dot{r}^2 - \dfrac{2a^2\sin\theta\cos\theta}{\Sigma}\dot{r}\dot{\theta} + \dfrac{4m\,a\,r\left(r\,\Sigma + m\left(r^2 - a^2\cos^2\theta\right)\right)\sin^2\theta}{\Sigma^2\left(r^2 + a^2\right)}\dot{r}\dot{\psi} - \dfrac{r\,\Delta}{\Sigma}\dot{\theta}^2 - \dfrac{\Delta\left(r\,\Sigma^2 - m\,a^2\left(r^2 - a^2\cos^2\theta\right)\sin^2\theta\right)\sin^2\theta}{\Sigma^3}\dot{\psi}^2 = 0

\ddot{\psi} + \dfrac{2m^2\,a\,r\left(r^2 - a^2\cos^2\theta\right)}{\Sigma^3\left(r^2 + a^2\right)}\dot{\tau}^2 + \dfrac{2m\,a\left(r^2 - a^2\cos^2\theta\right)\left(r^2 + a^2 + 2m\,r\right)}{\Sigma^2\left(r^2 + a^2\right)^2}\dot{\tau}\dot{r} - \dfrac{4m\,a\,r\cot\theta}{\Sigma^2}\dot{\tau}\dot{\theta} - \dfrac{4m^2\,a^2\,r\left(r^2 - a^2\cos^2\theta\right)\sin^2\theta}{\Sigma^3\left(r^2 + a^2\right)}\dot{\tau}\dot{\psi} + \dfrac{2m\,a\left(r^4 - a^4\cos^2\theta + m\,r^3 - m\,a^2\,r\cos^2\theta\right)}{\Sigma\left(r^2 + a^2\right)^3}\dot{r}^2 - \dfrac{4m\,a\,r\cot\theta}{\Sigma\left(r^2 + a^2\right)}\dot{r}\dot{\theta} + \dfrac{2r\,\Sigma^2\left(r^2 + a^2\right) - 2m\,a^2\left(3r^4 + a^2\,r^2\cos^2\theta + a^2\,r^2 - a^4\cos^2\theta\right)\sin^2\theta - 4m^2\,a^2\,r\left(r^2 - a^2\cos^2\theta\right)\sin^2\theta}{\Sigma^2\left(r^2 + a^2\right)^2}\dot{r}\dot{\psi} - \dfrac{2m\,a\,r^2}{\Sigma\left(r^2 + a^2\right)}\dot{\theta}^2 + \dfrac{2\left(\Sigma^2 + 2m\,a^2\,r\sin^2\theta\right)\cot\theta}{\Sigma^2}\dot{\theta}\dot{\psi} - \dfrac{2m\,a\,r\left(r\,\Sigma^2 - m\,a^2\left(r^2 - a^2\cos^2\theta\right)\sin^2\theta\right)\sin^2\theta}{\Sigma^3\left(r^2 + a^2\right)}\dot{\psi}^2 = 0
